findings.obligation: ACCT-03 requires inconsistent account snapshots to be rejected without silently coercing data.
findings.evidence: The normalizer accepts side='long' with market_value='-480.50' (and side='short' with positive market_value), then takes the absolute value and attributes exposure according only to side. Thus a contradictory broker snapshot is silently converted into plausible exposure instead of rejected. The checked-in fixture itself demonstrates the intended sign convention: long AAPL has positive market_value and short TSLA has negative market_value.
findings.consequence: Incorrectly sided or corrupted position data can produce a valid-looking long/short/gross exposure snapshot, undermining reconciliation inspection and downstream risk decisions.
findings.direction: Validate the signed market_value against position.side before computing exposure; reject contradictory snapshots and add both-direction fixture mutation cases.
